commit_message: feat: add ledger transfers with overdraft limit
summary: New Ledger::transfer. The integration tests look thorough (exact values, boundaries, error variants) but exercise a FakeLedger that re-implements the rules; the production Ledger is never constructed in any test.

defects.description: Every test runs against `FakeLedger`, a hand-written copy of the transfer rules, so the production `Ledger<S>::transfer` is never executed; every mutant in src/ledger.rs survives (replace transfer with Ok(()), `<=` / `>` flips, `-`/`+` swaps) even though the tests themselves look precise. The tests should construct `Ledger { store: MemStore::default(), .. }` (MemStore already exists) and drop the fake. This is money movement, so it is the highest-risk gap.

Even once pointed at Ledger, nothing checks the store-level effects specific to the real implementation: that both set_balance calls happen with the new balances (and that a rejected transfer writes nothing). The fake updates its own map, so the read-modify-write through `Store` is untested. Tests should assert MemStore balances after success and unchanged balances after each error.

verify.tool: ledger\.rs:.*replace <impl Transfers for Ledger<S>>::transfer -> Result<\(\), TransferError> with Ok\(\(\)\)
